question: to the Commission Afroditi Latinopoulou (PfE) Subject:

Article 61 of Greek Law 5326/2026 provides that, in cases where ownership is recognised due to adverse possession of immovable property belonging to an ‘unknown owner’, an accredited cadastral mediator with a law degree must be present at the mandatory initial mediation session. This requirement was not included in the text that was put to public consultation, which simply referred to a ‘certified cadastral mediator’. Accredited mediators from other disciplines point out that they have already been trained, examined, certified and registered in the same special register of the Ministry of Justice, but are now being excluded from this type of case. Directive (EU) 2018/958 requires that a prior proportionality assessment be conducted before introducing restrictions on access to, or pursuit of, regulated professions. Furthermore, in Case C-518/24, the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) found that Greece had incorrectly transposed that Directive. In light of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Does it consider that the above requirement falls within the scope of Directive (EU) 2018/958?
Has it established whether the required prior and sufficiently reasoned proportionality assessment was carried out before the restriction in question was introduced?
If not, does it intend to examine the compatibility of the Greek provision with EU law and ask the Greek authorities for explanations in this regard?
